subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was a Keeper of the Tome who was writing in blue ink on *The Discoveries* at the time of his death, with blackened fingertip and lower lip, and a chipped front tooth from a forward fall.
source_quote: Janussi had been taking notes when this happened. Writing hand, fresh stains. A man interrupted at work.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi had a broken nose and bruising that formed before death, indicating an assault occurred between dinner and his murder.
source_quote: The bruising around the broken nose held its color, dark and settled, the way bruising only sits when blood was still moving when it formed.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi’s tongue and left forefinger were blackened with a substance darker than ink, and the same smudge was on his lower lip, indicating ingestion and deliberate contact with a poison.
source_quote: The tip of his left forefinger was blackened. Not blue. Darker than blue. And the same dark smudge sat dead-center on his lower lip.

subject: Keeper's Chamber
fact: The Keeper's Chamber contained a silver pedestal, an ebony pipe with cherry tobacco, and an open safe with scattered empty pouches, loose sapphires, and scraps of parchment naming spells.
source_quote: A silver pedestal by the desk, an ebony pipe finely carved, cherry tobacco... Empty pouches scattered in front of it, sapphires loose and dazzling, scraps of parchment naming spells.

subject: Keeper's Chamber
fact: The safe still held four sealed pouches with sapphires, a figurine of a raven, a potion of supreme healing, a potion of water breathing, five diamonds, a heap of platinum and gold — all untouched.
source_quote: Still inside the safe were four sealed pouches, each with its sapphire — and beside them a figurine of a raven, a potion of supreme healing, another of water breathing, five diamonds each worth a fortune, a heap of platinum and gold, a small treasury left untouched.

subject: locket
fact: A locket was removed from Janussi’s neck, leaving two broken lead links on his skin, worn where it had hung for a long time.
source_quote: The impression of a chain on the back and sides, and beneath it two broken lead links. Something had hung there, and someone had torn it off him.

subject: *The Discoveries*
fact: *The Discoveries* was the last book Janussi was writing in, with fresh blue ink noting unfamiliar spells and their potential casting methods.
source_quote: The blue ink on *The Discoveries* had been laid down after the blue ink on another book. *The Golden Ass.* 'So that's the last thing he was writing?' Confirmation.

subject: armchair
fact: The armchair had three circular impacts and two holes punched clean through the back, consistent with darts of pure force, but no matching wounds on the body.
source_quote: Three circular impacts, horsehair stuffing scattered, two holes punched clean through the chair back. Darts of pure force.

subject: Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore
fact: A three-foot marble statue of the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore, holding a candle aloft, had been knocked over — not by magic, but by shock when the body was discovered.
source_quote: The statue had simply fallen... A scholar discovers a murdered keeper with his heart cut out and reaches blindly for the wall and the wall is a statue.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, an ooze from the Underdark, was given the black substance from Janussi’s lip and finger, but could not identify it — confirming its unnatural and dangerous nature.
source_quote: We gave him the substance. He gave it his best. It wasn't enough — a thin first effort, then a second pass with help, and still nothing he could name.

subject: murder sequence
fact: Janussi was assaulted, breaking his nose, then returned to his desk to write, ingested a black poison while reading, fell face-first, chipping his tooth, and was later rolled over and had his heart removed by a deliberate, unhurried killer.
source_quote: A man at his books, wetting his finger to turn a poisoned page. The black climbing through him while he read on, suspecting nothing. A fall, forward, hard — a broken nose, a chipped tooth on the stone. And then the patient hands arriving after, in no hurry at all, rolling the body and opening the chest to make certain he stayed gone.

subject: safe breach
fact: The safe was opened without force, and only one sapphire and one parchment were taken — the rest of a king’s ransom left untouched — indicating the thief sought a specific component, not wealth.
source_quote: Whoever did this came in, took one sapphire, and walked past a king's ransom.

subject: tobacco use
fact: Cherry tobacco was lit in the ebony pipe to mask the smell of poison, suggesting the killer or someone present was attempting to conceal the nature of the death.
source_quote: Tobacco smoke would hide the smell of poison. Of course it would.

subject: Keeper's Desk
fact: The desk held *The Discoveries*, *The Golden Ass*, blue ink, and evidence of multiple ink colors, with the latest writing in blue on *The Discoveries*.
source_quote: In the middle of the desk sat a spellbook. *The Discoveries.* Beside it, blue ink, fresh enough that it had a sequence to it.

subject: black substance
fact: The black substance on Janussi’s finger, lip, and tongue was not ink, not poison that Glabbagool recognized, and was deliberately used to contaminate the reader — implying it was sentient or magical.
source_quote: The skill wasn't in identifying the substance. It was in knowing, with certainty, what it was *not*.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz performed a forensic reading of the body, noting the tempo of the killer, the sequence of injuries, and the nature of the black substance.
source_quote: I logged that. *The first thing to read is the tempo of the killer.* This one had time.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum established the timeline of the assault using bruising patterns, confirming the broken nose occurred before death and identifying the chain marks from a removed locket.
source_quote: My focus narrowed and held, and the picture came clear and certain: this happened before he died. Not the fall. Earlier.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir identified the sequence of ink usage, confirming that Janussi’s final act was writing in *The Discoveries*, and noted the literary homage in the notes.
source_quote: The blue ink on *The Discoveries* had been laid down after the blue ink on another book. *The Golden Ass.* 'So that's the last thing he was writing?' Confirmation.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin questioned the candle on the statue out of fear of magical awakening, revealing his past trauma and causing Tadric to panic.
source_quote: Are you sure this — is it true about candles?

subject: statue fall
fact: The statue of the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore fell when the scholar discovered the body, proving it was an accident, not sabotage.
source_quote: The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had knocked it over in shock when he found the body at dawn.

subject: Keeper's Chamber
fact: The chamber showed no signs of forced entry, and the safe was opened cleanly — indicating the killer had access or knowledge of the combination.
source_quote: Open, but undamaged. No forced entry. The killer had the combination, or had no need of one.

subject: blue ink
fact: Blue ink on *The Discoveries* was fresher than on *The Golden Ass*, indicating Janussi was actively researching unfamiliar spells at the time of death.
source_quote: There was more than one color on those pages, and I wanted the newest one isolated before anything else.

subject: chipped tooth
fact: The chipped front tooth was jagged and recent, caused by Janussi falling face-first onto stone after being poisoned, not by violence.
source_quote: He had fallen forward. Face-first. Chipped the tooth on the way down.

subject: blackened fingertip
fact: The blackened fingertip and lip were not from ink, but from a substance that mimicked ink but was darker, more dangerous, and likely sentient — a reading poison.
source_quote: That was the entire point of the long look — not that the finger was stained, but that the stain was *wrong*.

subject: poison ingestion
fact: Janussi ingested the black substance by wetting his fingertip to turn pages, indicating the poison was embedded in the parchment and designed to be absorbed through touch and ingestion.
source_quote: Finger to a page, finger to the lip — turning pages, wetting the fingertip the way readers do without thinking, a hundred times an hour, never once considering that the page might be the thing reading *them*.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi carried a locket always, never took it off, and kept his chamber thick with tobacco smoke to medicate his failing lungs, living inside a haze on purpose.
source_quote: Janussi held one of the two keys of the Hightower Library, carried it always, never took it off, kept his chamber thick with it, medicated his failing lungs with the smell of it, lived inside a haze on purpose

subject: Daral Yashenti
fact: Daral Yashenti had been at Janussi's throat for years, drank excessively, shouted at Janussi twice in one day, called him 'nothing but a glorified book peddler,' and fled the second argument in terror.
source_quote: Daral Yashenti... those two have been at each other's throats for years... he drinks way too much... 'You're not fit to be the candle keep's keeper'... 'nothing but a glorified book peddler'... he ran away so fast

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas, a tiefling Curator of the Infernal Fortress, screamed at Janussi calling him a traitor, was seen glowing red in candlelight at 2–3 a.m. carrying a lantern she had no use for, and had incurred his wrath that morning.
source_quote: Sylvira Savikas... gave me the heebie-jeebies... screamed that Janussi was a traitor... glowing red in the candlelight... carrying a lantern... she can see in the dark without any light at all

subject: Hightower Library
fact: The Hightower Library has two keys — one held by Janussi, missing from his neck, and one held by the gate warden Kalan.
source_quote: Janussi held one of the two keys of the Hightower Library... the other key is heralded by the gate warden, Kalan

subject: the locket
fact: The locket was missing from Janussi’s neck — he carried it always, never took it off, and it was the only thing gone from the room.
source_quote: The locket was missing. Off Janussi's neck. And that knocked something loose in his memory... Janussi carried it always, never took it off

subject: the black residue
fact: Black residue was on the man’s mouth and fingers — definitively not from the blue ink, and came from somewhere the blue ink did not.
source_quote: The black on the man's mouth came from somewhere the blue ink did not... Black. Definitively not the blue ink — Grygum had already settled that, checked it twice and certain

subject: the gift tag
fact: The gift tag read: 'To Janussi, read it and weep, you old snob, a proper Dead Winter gift, your loving rival.' Written in a cramped, sour hand, by someone who resented the act of writing it.
source_quote: 'To Janussi, read it and weep, you old snob, a proper Dead Winter gift, your loving rival.'... cramped, sour hand... script of someone who resented the act of writing it

subject: the comedy book
fact: The comedy book — *The Golden Ass* — was annotated with jokes and obscure spell notes in the same hand and fresh ink, then vanished from the room, leaving only its absence as proof it had been there.
source_quote: *The Golden Ass* was a comedy... writing down jokes he found funny... blue ink captures both notes on obscure spells and jokes?... the same hand, the same fresh ink... the comedy book had walked out of the room... you do not annotate a thing you do not hold

subject: the murder chamber
fact: The murder chamber was filled with tobacco smoke — a habit Janussi kept to mask his failing lungs — and now served as the site where the smell of poison was hidden.
source_quote: A man who fills his own room with smoke as a habit... The one thing that tobacco smoke would do is hide the smell of poison... you fill a room with smoke to keep him from smelling what's already there

subject: the midnight thud
fact: At midnight, Hollypocket heard a thud from above — the last sound she associated with Janussi being alive — and later recalled seeing Sylvira Savikas’s glowing red face in candlelight, carrying a lantern she had no use for.
source_quote: I heard a thud upstairs... I swear I could see that devil woman's — Sylvira Savikas's — face glowing red in the candlelight... she was carrying a lantern. She's a tiefling, and she can see in the dark without any light at all

subject: the argument with Teles Ahvoste
fact: Teles Ahvoste shouted 'hypocrite' at Janussi during their meeting around the ninth bell, ending in a shouting match.
source_quote: I did hear Teles shout, *hypocrite*, at poor Janussi before he stormed out

subject: the argument with Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch passed Hollypocket on the steps with a face like thunder, nearly knocking the tea tray out of her hands.
source_quote: I passed Kalan Strongbranch on the steps. He had a face like thunder, nearly knocked the tray out of my hands

subject: the confrontation with Daral at half past ten
fact: Daral Yashenti returned drunk at half past ten, pounded on Janussi’s door until let in, argued loudly, then fled down the stairs in terror — the fastest Janussi had ever seen him run.
source_quote: Daral came back at half past ten, drunk as a skunk, pounding on the door until Janussi let him in... another loud argument, then the slam and the great reader running back down the stairs... I'd never seen him run away so fast

subject: the gift delivery
fact: A gift was delivered to Janussi — a Dead Winter gift inscribed by a rival — written in a resentful, cramped hand, and left in the wastebasket.
source_quote: A gift tag surfaced from the wastebasket... 'To Janussi, read it and weep, you old snob, a proper Dead Winter gift, your loving rival.'

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris, the assistant, identified Daral Yashenti as Janussi’s long-time rival and revealed that Janussi held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library.
source_quote: Fembris... 'Oh, that'll be Daral Yashenti. Those two have been at each other's throats for years.'... 'Janussi held one of the two keys of the Hightower Library.'

subject: Hollypocket
fact: Hollypocket, the housekeeper, witnessed all major confrontations with Janussi, heard the midnight thud, and saw Sylvira Savikas glowing red in candlelight carrying a lantern she had no use for.
source_quote: Hollypocket... brought the keeper his morning tea... heard Teles shout 'hypocrite'... overheard Daral calling him 'glorified book peddler'... heard the midnight thud... saw Sylvira Savikas’s face glowing red... carrying a lantern... she can see in the dark without any light at all

subject: Daz
fact: Daz, the Stonespeaker, used his crystal to prepare to interrogate the housecat — the only living witness in the chamber — and was the first to notice the significance of Sylvira’s lantern.
source_quote: Daz... 'I think I can talk to the cat.'... 'Talking to beasts, yeah. It's part of what the stone speaker crystal grants me.'... Daz was paying the weeping woman no attention whatsoever... 'That explains the candle.'

subject: the Garden Shadow
fact: The Garden Shadow had a saying about absence — that a room tells you most by what it is missing — possibly echoed by Brother Tharusk, the tall one who always smelled of incense.
source_quote: The Garden Shadow had a saying about that — or possibly Brother Tharusk did, the tall one who always smelled of incense

subject: the poison hypothesis
fact: The poison hypothesis emerged from the absence of the book, the black residue, the smoke, and the locket — all pointing to a murder masked by environmental concealment.
source_quote: The black on the pages of a book that was no longer in the room. The smoke that hid the smell of it... The one thing that tobacco smoke would do is hide the smell of poison... you don't fill a room with smoke to kill a man — you fill a room with smoke to keep him from smelling what's already there

subject: the cipher hypothesis
fact: The cipher hypothesis arose from the annotated comedy book — jokes and spell notes in the same hand, suggesting the book itself was a key to a replacement cipher.
source_quote: There's something written in the book that wasn't part of the original book — or maybe he's using the book and the notes to do some sort of cipher. Some sort of replacement cipher, and there's, like, some sort of code that the book ends up being the key to.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch, the gate warden, holds the second key to the Hightower Library and was seen with a face like thunder the morning of the murder.
source_quote: the other key is heralded by the gate warden, Kalan... He had a face like thunder, nearly knocked the tray out of my hands

subject: Teles Ahvoste
fact: Teles Ahvoste shouted 'hypocrite' at Janussi during their meeting, ending in a shouting match.
source_quote: I did hear Teles shout, *hypocrite*, at poor Janussi before he stormed out

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir was the one who noted the significance of Sylvira’s lantern and the connection between the candlelight and the poison’s concealment.
source_quote: That explains the candle.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum insisted on interviewing the housekeeper to determine what was missing — grounding the investigation in physical absence rather than political motive.
source_quote: One thing we need is somebody who knows what should be here, so they can tell us if anything's missing... go find, say, the housekeeper, and ask her, what is missing or out of place

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin connected the gift tag to the rivalry theory and identified the black residue as inconsistent with the blue ink, reinforcing the poison hypothesis.
source_quote: Okay, so that supports my theory. Some sort of rival gave him a gift, but it was sort of like a bitter thing... Black. Definitively not the blue ink

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recognized the significance of the lantern carried by Sylvira Savikas — a tiefling who needs no light — and was the first to link it to the candlelight as a cover for poison.
source_quote: That explains the candle.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep’s culture — not the library, but the scholars — is defined by grudges filed like scrolls, polished over years, and deployed as weapons.
source_quote: I despise this whole place a little — not Candlekeep, Candlekeep's fine, the books are fine — but the *culture* of it, the scholars who keep grudges the way a dragon keeps gold, sitting on them for years, polishing them

subject: the discovery of the missing book
fact: The comedy book — *The Golden Ass* — was confirmed missing from the room, its absence the only physical change, and its annotations the only evidence of its presence.
source_quote: the comedy book had walked out of the room... you do not annotate a thing you do not hold... And now it was gone, and it was the only thing gone

subject: the final hypothesis
fact: The final hypothesis combined poison, cipher, and rivalry — the book was a cipher key, the smoke concealed poison, the locket was stolen to implicate a rival, and Daral and Sylvira were the prime suspects.
source_quote: The poison and the cipher could both be true. The missing book carried both. We had read the room down to what it was willing to give. The rest of it lived somewhere else, and we'd have to go find it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is relieved that someone else has taken an expense off his account.
source_quote: Well, that saves me money on potions," said Grygum, relieved — someone else had just taken an expense off his account.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie is a five-year-old sleet-grey cat who is entirely uninterested in being disturbed and announced, 'I did not order any more ticklers!'
source_quote: The cat introduced herself, after a fashion. Queenie — five years old, sleet-grey, and entirely uninterested in being disturbed. "I did not order any more ticklers!" she announced, stretching.

subject: armchair
fact: Queenie settled into Janussi's armchair for a nap, only to be rudely awakened thirty minutes later by Sylvira Savikas blasting the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light.
source_quote: She had settled into Janussi's armchair for a nap, she said, "only to be rudely awakened some thirty minutes later by our Sylvira Savikas, this is in the morning, blasting the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light."

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas is a tiefling who blasted the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light, initiating a lover's quarrel with Janussi.
source_quote: Sylvira the tiefling, and Janussi, an on-and-off-again relationship. A lover's quarrel, then, opened with a flung working of force.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi is in an on-and-off-again relationship with Sylvira Savikas and owned an armchair where Queenie napped.
source_quote: Sylvira the tiefling, and Janussi, an on-and-off-again relationship. A lover's quarrel, then, opened with a flung working of force.

subject: armchamber
fact: The armchamber was blasted with a lance of unerring force light by Sylvira Savikas.
source_quote: blasting the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noted that the victim was still alive when Daral left, and the timeline held.
source_quote: "But the victim was still alive when Daral left," Thorin noted, and the timeline held. Yes. Daral exited with the book, and the dead man was not yet dead.

subject: The Golden Ass
fact: The Golden Ass is a book, dull enough to hold a person motionless and uninterested in scratching a cat, taken by Daral.
source_quote: "The Golden Ass", the missing volume, walking out of the room under Daral's arm.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral carried The Golden Ass under his arm and ran downstairs with a hypnotic block.
source_quote: when I later saw him run downstairs with a hypnotic block.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir said, "Oh, it's a TV!" — not quite the deduction but arrived at the same destination.
source_quote: "Oh, it's a TV!" said Zalthir, which was not quite the deduction but arrived at the same destination.

subject: Fheminor
fact: Fheminor is the short-legged one, the first guest to arrive in the evening.
source_quote: first Fheminor, *the short-legged one*, and later Daral, *the stinky breath one*.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is the stinky breath one, the second guest to arrive in the evening.
source_quote: first Fheminor, *the short-legged one*, and later Daral, *the stinky breath one*.

subject: corridor
fact: Queenie retreated to the corridor after Daral's shouting.
source_quote: she retreated to the corridor — "when I later saw him run downstairs with a hypnotic block."

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira appeared as a torn demon lady descending the steps, but did not smell like the demon lady.
source_quote: She'd prowled the nighttime cycle and seen *the torn demon lady* coming down the steps — Sylvira's shape — "But she didn't smell like the demon lady, though."

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie said, "Every time they open that block," they just sit there and don't tickle! — revealing The Golden Ass as a book that immobilizes.
source_quote: "Every time they open that block," Queenie said, "they just sit there and don't tickle!"

subject: locket
fact: The locket is intimate; Janussi carried it all the time and never took it off, though Queenie did not know what it was.
source_quote: The locket itself is intimate. He carried it all the time. He never took it off.

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris supplied that Janussi held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library.
source_quote: Fembris, *by golly*, supplied the column I was missing: Janussi held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan is the gate warden who holds the other key to the Hightower Library.
source_quote: The other key, I learned, rested with Kalan, the gate warden.

subject: Hightower Library
fact: The Hightower Library is the location whose contents were deleted from a book no one should have touched, likely due to unauthorized access with one of the two keys.
source_quote: That might explain why that stuff got deleted off that book that no one should have touched. Someone snuck in.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie assessed two-leggers: "I try to hold my breath whenever a two-legger passes. It's clear that you hardly ever lick yourselves at all. I've met cleaner dogs in my time."
source_quote: "How would I know? I try to hold my breath whenever a two-legger passes. It's clear that you hardly ever lick yourselves at all. I've met cleaner dogs in my time."

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie ended the interaction by saying, "You may now leave, and please give yourself a proper licking before returning to my tower."
source_quote: "You may now leave," she said, "and please give yourself a proper licking before returning to my tower."
